name: Coconut oil
summary: Coconut oil is the fat pressed from the flesh of coconuts, solid in a cool kitchen and used for cooking and on skin. This page lists what people say coconut oil does; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: Coconut oil is a rich source of medium-chain fatty acids, and it is very high in saturated fat. A 2021 overview describes its composition and how extraction methods differ.
The UK food table (CoFID) measures coconut oil at 899 kcal and 99.9 g of fat per 100 g, with 86.5 g of it saturated, 0.66 mg of vitamin E, and no protein, sugars, fibre or minerals.

For comparison, the same table measures fresh coconut flesh at 351 kcal and 36 g of fat per 100 g (31.4 g saturated), with 370 mg of potassium and 41 mg of magnesium. The oil does not carry those minerals.
processing: Coconut oil is not the same food as coconut flesh or coconut milk: the table's flesh has 36 g of fat per 100 g and the oil 99.9 g, so figures for one do not carry over to the other.
The 2021 overview describes the composition and properties of coconut oils extracted by different methods, such as virgin and refined; this page cannot say which is healthier.

whoShouldBeCareful.with: High LDL cholesterol or heart disease
whoShouldBeCareful.note: A 2020 meta-analysis of 16 trials found that coconut oil raised LDL cholesterol by 10.5 mg/dL and HDL cholesterol by 4.0 mg/dL compared with non-tropical vegetable oils, and concluded that coconut oil results in significantly higher LDL cholesterol. If your cholesterol is high or you have heart disease, talk to your doctor.

A 1999 report describes two people with life-threatening tree nut allergy who reacted to coconut, with antibodies that recognised proteins shared by coconut and walnut. This is two patients; it does not say how common this is, and oil is not the same as the flesh. If you react to nuts, talk to your doctor or an allergist.

unknowns: Whether coconut oil changes heart attacks or strokes: the trials measured blood fats and other risk markers, not these outcomes.
Why the trials disagree on HDL and LDL: the meta-analysis found a lot of difference between studies (I2 of 84 % for LDL), and this page does not resolve it.
What coconut oil did in the writings of ancient Greece and Rome: coconut was not known to them in a text this page could open and read, so no older beliefs are listed.
